title: Math · Grade 6
description: An original starter path: build the idea, work an example, then try it. A focused introduction, ready to grow with your class.
framework: Original introductory mathematics practice; suggested grade placement, not a complete standards syllabus.
sequenceNote: Suggested teaching sequence, not mandated unit order.
alignmentNote: Starter course; not full grade-level coverage.

lessons.title: Ratios compare
lessons.reading: A ratio compares quantities in a stated order. Equivalent ratios multiply both quantities by the same factor.
lessons.easyReading: A ratio compares quantities in a stated order. Equivalent ratios multiply both quantities by the same factor.
lessons.expertReading: A ratio compares quantities in a stated order. Equivalent ratios multiply both quantities by the same factor. A part-to-part ratio differs from a part-to-whole fraction.
lessons.worked: Two red beads for every three blue beads gives a red-to-blue ratio of 2:3.
steps: Two red beads for every three blue beads gives a red-to-blue ratio of 2:3.

application.prompt: A 2:3 ratio has 8 red beads. How many blue beads?
application.explanation: 12. A ratio compares quantities in a stated order. Equivalent ratios multiply both quantities by the same factor.

vocab.definition: A comparison of two quantities by division.

lessons.practice: Explain how ratio helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 12. A ratio compares quantities in a stated order. Equivalent ratios multiply both quantities by the same factor.

lessons.title: Find a unit rate
lessons.reading: A unit rate gives a quantity per one unit of another quantity. Divide to make the second quantity one.
lessons.easyReading: A unit rate gives a quantity per one unit of another quantity. Divide to make the second quantity one.
lessons.expertReading: A unit rate gives a quantity per one unit of another quantity. Divide to make the second quantity one. Units identify what the quotient measures and help prevent reversed ratios.
lessons.worked: A 180-mile trip in three hours averages 60 miles per hour.
steps: A 180-mile trip in three hours averages 60 miles per hour.

application.prompt: A four-pack costs $10. What is the price per item?
application.explanation: $2.50. A unit rate gives a quantity per one unit of another quantity. Divide to make the second quantity one.

vocab.definition: A rate expressed per one unit of another quantity.

lessons.practice: Explain how unit rate helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: $2.50. A unit rate gives a quantity per one unit of another quantity. Divide to make the second quantity one.

lessons.title: Integers on a line
lessons.reading: Negative numbers lie left of zero and positive numbers lie right. A number farther right is greater.
lessons.easyReading: Negative numbers lie left of zero and positive numbers lie right. A number farther right is greater.
lessons.expertReading: Negative numbers lie left of zero and positive numbers lie right. A number farther right is greater. Absolute value measures distance from zero and is always nonnegative.
lessons.worked: −2 is greater than −5 because −2 lies farther right on the number line.
steps: −2 is greater than −5 because −2 lies farther right on the number line.

application.explanation: −1. Negative numbers lie left of zero and positive numbers lie right. A number farther right is greater.

vocab.definition: A whole-number value or its negative, including zero.

lessons.practice: Explain how integer helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: −1. Negative numbers lie left of zero and positive numbers lie right. A number farther right is greater.

lessons.title: Expressions and equations
lessons.reading: An expression represents a quantity; an equation states equality. Substitute a value for every occurrence of the variable.
lessons.easyReading: An expression represents a quantity; an equation states equality. Substitute a value for every occurrence of the variable.
lessons.expertReading: An expression represents a quantity; an equation states equality. Substitute a value for every occurrence of the variable. Substitution must preserve the expression’s operation order.

application.explanation: 17. An expression represents a quantity; an equation states equality. Substitute a value for every occurrence of the variable.

vocab.definition: A symbol representing a number that can vary or be unknown.

lessons.practice: Explain how variable helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 17. An expression represents a quantity; an equation states equality. Substitute a value for every occurrence of the variable.

lessons.title: Keep an equation balanced
lessons.reading: Apply the same operation to both sides of an equation. Undo the operation on the unknown to isolate it.
lessons.easyReading: Apply the same operation to both sides of an equation. Undo the operation on the unknown to isolate it.
lessons.expertReading: Apply the same operation to both sides of an equation. Undo the operation on the unknown to isolate it. Equivalent equations have the same solution set.
lessons.worked: For x + 7 = 19, subtract seven from both sides to get x = 12.
steps: For x + 7 = 19, subtract seven from both sides to get x = 12.

application.explanation: x = 23. Apply the same operation to both sides of an equation. Undo the operation on the unknown to isolate it.

vocab.definition: A value that makes an equation true.

lessons.practice: Explain how solution helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: x = 23. Apply the same operation to both sides of an equation. Undo the operation on the unknown to isolate it.
